content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I want to retrieve values stored in the registers of [product_name], for example, counter values. I'm using [product_name] software and selecting Tools > Transfer > I/O status. Is there a way to access registry values directly? Any help would be appreciated.
If you can provide more details about your specific goal, that might help us assist you better.

With the menu Transfer > I/O status, you can only view certain listed values—inputs, outputs, markers, and timers. Some analog values can be seen using analog markers, but this isn't practical for counters. To view the values of elements like timers, counters, and analog components, you would need to use VM mapping through Tools > Parameter VM mapping. You can assign analog network inputs in your program to these mappings and connect them to an analog marker, which then shows in I/O status. Note that counter values are 32-bit, while analog markers are only 16-bit including sign, which creates limitations. Alternatively, with newer [product_name] controllers, activating the internal web server allows you to log in and select variables (including VM types like DWORD), and you can create messages with counter values to display directly in virtual displays via the web server. Best regards, [user_name].
Thank you, that's very helpful! Do you have any sample methods for extracting counter values? That would be really useful.
Are you looking for an example like this?
Or you could follow the approach suggested by [user_name].

It would help if you explain exactly what you want to achieve. Are you aiming to log a counter value continuously into a CSV file? If that's the case, you can use [product_name] to create a CSV file on a micro SD card using the data logging block. Alternatively, you can try the free additional [product_name] software called [product_name] Access Tool, but your PC with Excel must remain connected the entire time.

This approach is straightforward and sufficient for the task! Is it possible to obtain I/O status for multiple controllers online simultaneously—that is, generate separate CSV files for several controllers at once?

Please describe your job in more detail. What exactly do you need to monitor, and how many variables are involved? When [product_name] controllers are connected over LAN, you can collect data at a central master and display I/O statuses from several controllers, but viewing is limited to one at a time. Other possibilities depend on your hardware, number of variables, and variable types. Regards, [user_name].
I've requested further details from the topic starter here and in another thread, but it seems they're unable or unwilling to clarify what they want to do.

Sure, I'll try to explain in more depth: 1) I plan to connect multiple [product_name] controllers to a central workstation via VPN (with static IP addresses). 2) I want to gather some inputs and flags using Tools > Transfer > I/O status, and save them as CSV files automatically. My question: Is it possible to collect I/O data from several [product_name] controllers and create a separate CSV file for each simultaneously?

Unfortunately, I don't see sufficient details provided. However, if you have access to all [product_name] controllers, you can run multiple instances of [product_name] software to obtain values from several controllers. You might want to try it. Regards, [user_name].

You can consider using a [product_name] API middleware server. [url] Your [product_name] controller must be accessible via the internet. You'll be able to read data from inputs, markers, and analog points, and trigger function keys, depending on your [product_name] program's configuration. Use a key format to retrieve data: [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are looking for effective methods to extract and observe register and counter values from [product_name] controllers, particularly using [product_name] configuration software. Existing options for reading I/O status do not fully cover block values like counters due to technical limitations. There is a clear demand for easier and more direct ways to log such values, especially when monitoring several controllers at the same time—whether via CSV logging, web interfaces, or middleware solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect solutions that allow them to effortlessly access and record internal values, such as counters, ideally in analyzable formats like CSV, and to do so across multiple controllers concurrently, with minimal complexity.
